improvements: GAS bound once per read (finding 1 fixed); the 7 rotated SELECT loops (`while not ext_call.success`, P3) are now plain `while True` loops with no first iteration before them; ~250 `revert with memory from mem[64]` copies of return data now print as `revert with ext_call.return_data[...]`, with guard-first `if not ext_call.success`; 21 custom errors decoded (0x784cb7b8, 0x3351b260, 0x4c085bf1); calls whose selector came from memory are now named (swap x9, metadata() x9, permitTransferFrom, unknowncd0cc1ce, unknownf3cd914c, unknown4dcebcba); `return memory from mem[64]` -> `return 1`; dead restores (`mem[52] = 0`, `mem[448 len 96] = 0`) dropped; P6 32 -> 0, P2 170 -> 163; 1,289 fewer lines.
notes: Reviewed by structure (33k-line diff, mostly renumbering and hex padding). Normalized variable numbers and hex, canonicalized the two benign old forms (return-data revert via mem[64], success-first if), then compared per function the multisets of calls, reverts, transient writes, returns and aborts: every difference is explained by the named selectors, decoded errors, `return 1`, the 3 SELECT first-iteration copies per function removed by the unrotation, and abort markers merged into aborted joins. Loop counts unchanged (52 while: 8 actions-loop copies, 19 while True, hop loops); balanceOf unchanged. The 67 `revert with memory from uint24(..)` after a failed transfer (pointer read from the clobbered free-memory word) are unchanged. Old 13370 / new 12599: a SELECT first call whose arm ends with no success check is the same in both texts (its join is aborted).
summary: No semantic regression: the GAS finding is fixed, the SELECT loops are unrotated, return-data reverts, custom errors, selectors and the bool return are much clearer; the only worse spot is a revert's token argument now shown as a raw memory slice (low). Coverage, tail duplication and arithmetic findings remain.
